plot: One bright autumn morning Big Bertha keeps driving past her bus stop and says the stop, the school and the bakery all moved in the night; Turbo is cleared (too slow from slow-race practice to be sneaky), Bolt and Pip find the stop's bolts rusty and the grass unsquashed, and when Bertha says good morning to a trash bin and reads BAKERY as 'BUNNY SHOP', Pip remembers she called Bolt a mailbox last night, and Bolt reveals nothing moved: far things look blurry to Bertha; she is embarrassed, but Grumpy shows his own reading glasses, Doctor Dottie fits Bertha with glasses for far away, and she sees every autumn leaf; then she spots a little car with a red scarf on the hill, waving at Bolt.

script.title: Someone Moved Bertha's Bus Stop!
script.description: Big Bertha says her bus stop moved in the night. Inspector Bolt finds out what really changed. Inspector Bolt #37

set.place: Wheelburg school road with the yellow bus stop post by the school gate, Bakery Lane and Doctor Dottie's clinic by the park, a bright autumn morning

beats.say: Where is my bus stop?! It was right here yesterday!
Hold on, everybody! Big Bertha will find it!
Bertha, wait! You just drove past it! Again!
It was a bright autumn morning, the day after the squirrel mystery.
And Big Bertha said half of Wheelburg had moved in the night.
Good morning, Bertha. A bus stop that moves? Tell me more.
The stop! The school! The bakery! Everything moved, Bolt!
Nothing moved. I'd know. Moving things is my job.
Then why can't I find them? I drive here every day!
Procedure. We start where the stop always was.
And there by the school gate stood the yellow bus stop post.
It's here, Bertha! Right here! Look!
That? Sweetie, that's not my stop. That's a lamppost.
It's yellow. It says BUS STOP. It's your stop.
Then somebody moved it back! While we weren't looking! Sneaky!
Did somebody say SNEAKY? Agent Turbo, reporting for duty!
Turbo! Was it you? You love a funny trick!
Not me! I was doing slow practice all morning. Look!
Turbo rolled by. So slowly that a leaf landed on his roof.
He's telling the truth. Nobody could be that slow and sneaky.
Let's look at the ground. Clues don't move.
The post's bolts are old and rusty. Nobody has touched them.
And the grass around it isn't squashed at all!
So this post has not moved. Not for years.
But it looked SO different! It was all fuzzy and far!
If I can't find my stop, the kids can't find me!
Bertha felt worried. And a little bit embarrassed.
Come on, team. Let's check the bakery. Maybe that moved too.
So everyone drove down Bakery Lane together.
Good morning, Grumpy! Lovely day!
I'm behind you, Bertha. That's a trash bin.
Ha! Bertha said good morning to a trash bin!
It's grey and square! Just like Grumpy! Easy mistake!
I am not square.
Bolt, last night she called you a mailbox too.
Interesting. A mailbox. A lamppost. And now a trash bin.
Bolt, please. Who is moving my town around?
Bertha, can you read Benny's sign for me? From right there?
Of course! It says... BUNNY SHOP.
Bertha, it says BAKERY. In great big letters!
Bakery? But it looks all blurry from here.
Bolt rolled close to Bertha. And Bertha leaned in very close to him.
Oh! There you are, Bolt. You're so sharp up close!
Nobody moved the town, Bertha. The town is right where it was.
It's your eyes. Far things look blurry to you now.
My eyes? No, no. Big buses have perfect eyes!
What will the kids think? A school bus who can't see?
Uh oh. If Bertha can't see, who drives the kids?
Bertha. I have something to show you.
Grumpy opened his little side box. Inside was a pair of glasses.
Reading glasses. Ten years now. Small words go fuzzy for me.
Grumpy wears GLASSES? I never knew that!
Nobody asked. They help me read my tow list.
And nobody laughed at you?
Turbo laughed once. Then he needed a tow.
That's true. He towed me anyway. Very kindly.
Bertha, let's see Doctor Dottie. She checks eyes too.
So everyone drove to Doctor Dottie's clinic by the park.
Hello, Bertha! Read the letters on my chart, please.
Big A. Then... a B? Or a bunny?
Just as I thought. You need glasses for far away.
Lots of grown-ups do. And lots of kids too!
Doctor Dottie fitted two big round glasses on Bertha's front.
Oh. Oh my. OH MY!
I can see every leaf! Red ones! Gold ones! Tiny ones!
And there's my bus stop! It never moved at all!
Bertha, you look so smart in glasses!
Like a professor bus! Professor Bertha!
Professor Bertha. I like that. Kids, all aboard!
Remember, everyone: needing help to see is nothing to hide.
And glasses look good on everyone. Even trash bins.
Bertha drove the kids to school. Straight to the stop. First try.
First try! Ha! Thank you, Doctor Dottie! Thank you, Grumpy!
Then Bertha looked far away, up the hill road. And she stopped.
Bolt? There's a little car up on the hill. It's waving at you.
At me? Who would wave at me from up there?
I can see it so clearly now. It has a red scarf!
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
